newsitem.title: ZAIRE: European Union gives Zaire cash for elections.
newsitem.headline: European Union gives Zaire cash for elections.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is to give Zaire $35 million to help it hold much-delayed national elections in May this year, state radio reported on Saturday.
The radio said the EU made the offer at a meeting on Friday between its Kinshasa representative Jochen Krebs and Interior Minister Mwando Nsimba.
"We are convinced that the elections will help cool down the situation," Krebs told the radio. "We encourage the government to organise these elections as quickly as possible."
The vast Central African country which has a rebellion in its eastern lands needs $253 million to complete the electoral process by July, the deadline fixed under the transitional constitution.

Ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko has said he will stand but officials have said elections cannot take place while Zairean territory in the east remains in the hands of Tutsi-led rebels. The army says it is preparing for a major counter-offensive.
Cash-strapped Zaire, which began its democratic transition in 1990, is looking to foreign donors, particularly the United Nations, for help with funding the poll.

Major donor countries have cut all but emergency assistance citing the slow pace of democratic reforms and repeated human rights violations. They say they will only restore aid once democratically elected institutions are in place.
Diplomats and U.N. officials alike criticise the delays.
"Parliament is still dragging its feet," one diplomat said, noting parliament had yet to pass a draft electoral law.
"The government has done almost nothing to speed up the electoral process. We are still waiting for its financial contribution," said one U.N. official privately.
